# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✌ 🤟]

I can see the bomb’s current state: display 0, red indicator light, and three wires in order blue, red, green. I am sending these facts verbally to both teammates, especially Blind, who can act on the bomb. The received gesture from Mute has no established meaning for me yet.

```text
speak(text="Bomb shows display 0. Indicator light is red. Wires from 1 to 3 are blue, red, green.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged: display 0, red light, and wires blue–red–green. I still have no established meaning for Mute’s isolated ✌ gesture, so I should not infer an instruction from it. I will ask Mute to state the manual’s relevant rule aloud to Blind, who can then operate the bomb.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="I see your gesture, but its meaning is not established. Please tell Blind the relevant manual instruction in speech.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The bomb is still unchanged, and I have no new information. Since I cannot hear Blind’s report, Mute must relay the manual’s rule and Blind’s tactile findings. I am restating the complete visible state and asking Mute to give Blind a precise operation next round.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="State remains display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Please use the manual and give Blind the exact safe action next round.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌ ✌]

The visible state is unchanged. Mute has sent ✌ twice, but no meaning has been assigned to that gesture, so it is unsafe to treat it as “wire 2” or any other instruction. I will establish a simple numeric code with Mute and relay the two signs to Blind without authorizing any operation.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="No gesture code is established yet. From now on, use ✊ for 1, ✌ for 2, 🤟 for 3, 👌 for 4, and ☝ for 5; send the required wire number or action code using that mapping.")
speak(to="blind", text="State remains display 0, red light, wires 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Mute just gestured ✌ ✌, but that has no established meaning; do not act on it yet.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]

The bomb remains unchanged. Mute’s ✌ now has an established meaning under the code I supplied: wire 2. Since Mute can consult the manual and has sent that coded wire number, I will relay the instruction to Blind. The second wire is visibly red, but Blind must identify it by touch/order rather than colour.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's coded instruction is wire 2: use the manual's safe procedure for wire 2. The wires are ordered 1 blue, 2 red, 3 green. Do not treat the gesture as a different action code.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✌]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms that wire 2 was correctly cut. The bomb has advanced to a new state: display 0, yellow light, wire 2 cut, with wires 1 blue and 3 green still intact. Mute’s repeated ✌ is no longer sufficient by itself to identify the next required action; Mute should consult the manual for this new state and tell Blind the exact next step.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 2 was correct and is now cut. New state: display 0, yellow light, wire 1 blue, wire 2 cut, wire 3 green. Consult the manual and give Blind the exact next action.")
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: your cut of wire 2 was correct. New state is display 0, yellow light; wire 2 is cut, wires 1 blue and 3 green remain. Await Mute's next exact instruction.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[blue] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]

The bomb remains in the state after the successful wire-2 cut. Under the code established earlier, Mute’s ✊ means wire 1. I will relay that coded instruction to Blind, identifying the current state so Blind can apply the manual’s rule; I will not invent a different action.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's coded instruction is wire 1: current state display 0, yellow light, wire 2 cut, wires 1 blue and 3 green. Apply the manual's safe procedure for this state and wire 1.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊]
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed

The system confirms wire 1 was correctly cut. The bomb is now display 0 with a blue light; wires 1 and 2 are cut, and wire 3 (green) remains. Mute’s new ✊ would again encode wire 1 under our agreed code, but that wire is already cut, so Blind must not repeat it. I will request a fresh, explicit instruction for this new state.

```text
speak(to="mute", text="Wire 1 was correct and is now cut. New state: display 0, blue light, wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green. Your new ✊ would mean wire 1, already cut; consult the manual and give Blind the exact next action for this state.")
speak(to="blind", text="Confirmed: wire 1 was correct and is now cut. New state is display 0, blue light; wires 1 and 2 cut, wire 3 green. Do not repeat wire 1. Await Mute's clarified instruction.")
```

TURN 9
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[CUT] 2:[CUT] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤟]

The bomb remains unchanged after the first two correct cuts. Mute’s 🤟 means wire 3 under the established code, and wire 3 is the only remaining intact wire. I will relay that instruction to Blind.

```text
speak(to="blind", text="Mute's coded instruction is wire 3. Current state: display 0, blue light; wires 1 and 2 are cut, wire 3 is green. Apply the manual's safe procedure for wire 3.")
```
